section_summary.extract_value: This introduction presents a theoretical framework for understanding how body image flexibility may mediate the relationship between body dissatisfaction and body appreciation in a sample of White older adolescent females preparing for college. The study extends Webb et al.'s (2014) affect regulation model of positive body image by testing body image flexibility as a mediating variable across three models examining different types of body size discrepancies (personal ideal, cultural ideal, and peer comparison). The investigation aims to advance understanding of how negative and positive body image operate synergistically and to operationalize body dissatisfaction using multiple external comparison referents beyond the conventional personal ideal standard.
